primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency due to CYP17A1 loss of function
mechanism: CYP17A1 deficiency impairs cortisol and sex-steroid synthesis. Elevated ACTH diverts steroid precursors toward mineralocorticoid-active 11-deoxycorticosterone and corticosterone, causing hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis while androgen deficiency causes absent or delayed sexual development.
vignette: A 16-year-old girl is evaluated for primary amenorrhea and absent secondary sexual development. She has hypertension and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis. Plasma renin activity is suppressed, cortisol and sex steroids are low, and ACTH is elevated.
lead: Which of the following adrenal steroids is most likely increased in this patient?
distractor_notes: DHEA production requires 17-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase activity and is reduced in CYP17A1 deficiency.
Androstenedione is a sex-steroid precursor downstream of 17,20-lyase activity and is reduced.
17-hydroxyprogesterone formation requires 17α-hydroxylase activity and is not the mineralocorticoid-active steroid accumulating in this disorder.
Cortisol synthesis is impaired by CYP17A1 deficiency; elevated ACTH instead drives accumulation of mineralocorticoid-active precursors.
key_expl: 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency reduces cortisol and sex-steroid production. Loss of cortisol feedback raises ACTH, which increases synthesis along the mineralocorticoid pathway. 11-Deoxycorticosterone and corticosterone accumulate and cause hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis.
objective: Identify excess 11-deoxycorticosterone as the mineralocorticoid-active steroid driving hypertension in 17α-hydroxylase deficiency.
